title: uv makes Python installs fast
topic: uv, the Python package and project manager written in Rust

alternates: Your Python script won't run on a new laptop? One tool fixes that.
hook.headline: YOUR SCRIPT WON'T RUN?

story.promise: weather.py runs on a new laptop

facts.claim: uv is an extremely fast Python package and project manager, written in Rust, 10-100x faster than pip
uv is a single tool to replace pip, pip-tools, pipx, poetry, pyenv, twine, virtualenv, and more
uv automatically downloads missing Python versions as needed, so you do not need to install Python to get started
uv is disk-space efficient, with a global cache for dependency deduplication
uv add --script writes inline dependency metadata into a script, and uv run creates an environment with those dependencies

beats.narration: Normally you'd juggle pyenv, virtualenv and pip. uv does all three jobs.
beats.headline: 3 TOOLS, 1 COMMAND EACH

story.after: pyenv, venv and pip each replaced by one uv command: ONE TOOL REPLACES 3
story.action: the host types the three uv commands, one per old tool

beats.narration: First, uv add writes the packages your script needs right into the file.
beats.headline: UV ADD --SCRIPT

story.before: weather.py with no list of its packages
story.after: weather.py carries its dependencies: PACKAGES INSIDE THE FILE
story.action: the host runs uv add --script and the header block appears in the file

beats.narration: It installs them ten to a hundred times faster than pip, because it's written in Rust.
beats.headline: 10-100X FASTER THAN PIP

story.after: uv crosses the line while pip lags: 10-100X FASTER THAN PIP
story.action: the uv cart races past the pip cart to the finish

beats.narration: Every script shares one cache, so a package never downloads twice.
beats.headline: 1 CACHE FOR EVERY SCRIPT

story.before: every script downloads its own packages
story.after: all scripts pulled to 1 CACHE: NOTHING DOWNLOADS TWICE
story.action: the cache magnet pulls every script card in

beats.narration: Then uv run even fetches the right Python, and your script just runs.
beats.headline: UV RUN FETCHES PYTHON 3.13

story.before: weather.py still has no Python on the new laptop
story.after: uv run fetches Python 3.13 and weather.py prints the weather: IT RUNS
story.action: the host throws weather.py into the terminal and hits run

cta.narration: Comment UV and I'll send you the setup.

premises: A race between pip and uv: uv crosses the line first, then wins every lap as more packages pile on, and the crowd holds up 100X.
One script, weather.py, that will not run on a new laptop: it fails, needs three tools, gets its packages written into it, installs fast from a shared cache, and finally runs with one command.
A toolbox crammed with pyenv, virtualenv, pip and poetry: each tool is pulled out and dropped into one uv box until the toolbox is empty.
story.why: A broken script is the problem viewers actually have; it can fail on screen, travel through every set in the host's hand, change state each beat, and visibly run at the end.
story.object: weather.py, a Python script that will not run
story.spine: Your script fails on a new laptop. But fixing it normally takes three tools. Therefore uv does all three, and writes the packages into the script itself. Therefore installs are 10-100x faster, and a shared cache means nothing downloads twice. Until finally uv run fetches Python and the same script runs.
story.ending: The terminal that said BROKEN now prints the weather and stamps IT RUNS: WEATHER.PY RUNS.
